title: Why the show closed at the Mercury Theater
summary: The Mercury was bought out by concession owners Larry and Maggie Fields, renamed the Abbey Theater and leased to NYU, so the show lost its home.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Why don't you explain what happened with the show at the Mercury Theater.

Well, the Mercury Theater changed its name, see. The Mercury Theater was bought out by the concessioners there, which was Larry and Maggie Fields. It's known as the Abbey Theater now. And New York University has some leases on it, see. We have been invited to return, you see. Lady D. Bradley and the Chuck Green -- (Reminiscing with Chuck Green, you see, of Tap Happening and the Hoofers, you see.

And we haven't been into some works about this. And I mean, even this (unintelligible) this television producer of "What's My Line," and "To Tell The Truth." Mimi O'Brien. She told me about any other possibilities -- to be sure to let her know. And I've been in the process myself of letting her know, see, about these -- to tell the truth, you see.
Can you tell us what happened, why did the show close at the Mercury Theater?

Because they were bought out. The concessioners, Larry and Maggie Fields -- I'll repeat it again. They had a concession in the lobby of the Mercury Theater for the statesman from Westchester, you see. And they bought him out, see, and changed the name from Mercury to the Abbey, which it's called now. And as soon as they got this Abbey name, I mean New York University -- see, student bodies -- always studious -- they leased it for about -- I guess about four or five years, see, from the new owners, see.
So, it really had not to do with the performances being attended, but purely had to be -- had to deal with mismanagement?
Yes. Well, you could say that. I'd like to say repetory.
